claims.paraphrase: The specified operating supply range is 1.7 V through 1.95 V.
Voltage applied to any pin is limited to -0.6 V through VCC plus 0.4 V.

claims.section: 4.2 Serial Data Input, Output and IOs
claims.paraphrase: Standard SPI uses DI as the device input and DO as the device output, with CLK and chip select as device inputs.
The datasheet documents multiple package-specific pin configurations; a family name alone does not select one pinout.

documents.title: TXU0304 4-Bit Fixed Direction Voltage-Level Translator with Schmitt-Trigger Inputs and 3-State Outputs

facts.channel_topology: three A-to-B plus one B-to-A fixed-direction channels

claims.paraphrase: The pin table defines three A-side inputs driving B-side outputs and one B-side input driving an A-side output.
Both supply rails have a recommended operating range beginning at 1.08 V and extending to 5.5 V.
Driving output enable low places all translator outputs in their high-impedance state.
TI shows an SPI mapping, while explicitly treating application information as outside the component specification and requiring design validation.

documents.title: SN74AXC4T245 Four-Bit Bus Transceiver with Configurable Voltage Translation and Tri-State Outputs

claims.paraphrase: The four channels are split into two two-bit sections, each controlled by one shared direction input.
Both supply rails have a recommended operating range of 0.65 V through 3.6 V.
Each section's direction input selects A-to-B or B-to-A for that entire two-channel section.

supported_conclusions: Given a verified 1.8 V DUT supply and a host that actually drives 3.3 V, direct connection is outside the DUT datasheet any-pin absolute maximum.
The TXU0304 documented fixed-direction topology is structurally compatible with three host-to-DUT signals and one DUT-to-host signal.
A single SN74AXC4T245 cannot assign three channels in one direction and one in the opposite direction because direction is shared in two-channel groups.
TXU0304 may be advanced as the preferred translator-family candidate, but not as a fabrication-ready implementation.
